versions.name: RXV2-0.9.568-bank-putback2
versions.notes: Bank put-back, bench-proven on the Goblin and polished: a put-back no longer forgets which bank the phone had chosen (so a read arriving after a put-back really does get the phone's bank re-selected first), a save marks the flight controller's bank as unknown until re-read (Rotorflight re-applies the switch by itself right after every save), and the event log now says 'Boot banks saved back for the switch' when only the boot bank needed fixing.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.567-bank-putback
versions.notes: Banks go back to the transmitter's switch after a phone session. Rotorflight only re-applies a bank switch when the switch moves, so a tuning page that left the flight controller on another bank was flown on that bank until the switch moved. Now the receiver notes the switch's PID and rates banks before a page's first bank select, and 5 s after the phone goes quiet (transmitter off, disarmed) puts them back - and saves them as the boot banks if the session had saved on another bank. Never under a live transmitter (the switch owns the banks then; the event log says where the FC was left). Pages and apps see no difference: a request that arrives after a put-back gets its own bank re-selected first.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.566-restore-names
versions.notes: Restore from phone now names what it wrote (up to four items, then a count) and the Back up / Restore result stays on screen until the next run instead of vanishing after a few seconds. Needs app 4.18 (iPhone) / 4.10 (Android) for the names.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.565-restore-counts
versions.notes: Backup & restore page: the finishing line now says what a restore actually did - 'Checked N settings - the model already had every one. Nothing was written' when nothing differed, or how many were written and verified (needs app 4.17 / Android 4.09 for the counts). The 'keep the transmitter OFF' warning disappears when the run is over.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.564-msp52-bug
versions.notes: Fix for the missing volts and RPM after a save: a Rotorflight 4.6 bug - its adjustments list (MSP 52) is too big for its receiver-link buffer and the overflow wipes its own telemetry setup. The receiver now never asks for that list, refuses it from any app or script, spots any oversize answer and puts the saved-good telemetry setup back before any save. Also refused: writes that arrive with no data, factory reset and motor test over the link.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.563-telemetry-speed
versions.notes: Telemetry speed: a new card on the Rotorflight page sets Rotorflight's telemetry link rate to FAST (1000/1, the new default) or standard (250/8). Rotorflight paces its answers to the phone and the transmitter by that rate, so settings reads, backups and restores come back about six times quicker and volts/RPM update sooner. Applying restarts the flight controller (transmitter off). Telemetry-setup guard: the receiver keeps the last good sensor list (also across reboots), re-reads it every 30 s while idle, puts it back into the flight controller's RAM if it turns up empty, and checks it before every save from a page, the phone app or the transmitter - so an emptied list (no volts/RPM) can never be saved into the flight controller again. A restore from a phone backup keeps the flight controller's current telemetry speed. Also: a transmitter edit or arming-channel probe can no longer collide with a heartbeat probe (the FC answers the first request and drops the second), a larger serial buffer for the faster stream, and a restart asked for by a page now answers at once instead of a timeout.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.562-probe-holdoff
versions.notes: Fixes the other cause of "flight controller did not respond": the receiver's own 5-second FC heartbeat probe. Rotorflight answers the first request it finds in its buffer and throws the second away, so a probe fired between two page or app reads made the read behind it vanish (about 1 in 14 back-to-back reads). The probe now waits 1.2 s after any page/app reply. Pairs with 0.9.561 (slow chunked replies) - both are now fixed, so Back up, Restore and the Rotorflight pages should read cleanly.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.559-full-backup
versions.notes: The phone backup now covers the WHOLE Rotorflight setup, not just the tune: PIDs, advanced PIDs, rates, governor & rescue (every bank); mixer, servos, motor & gear ratio; arming switch & modes, channel map, receiver & failsafe (incl. per-channel failsafe values); battery, voltage & current meters, gyro filters & RPM notches, board/gyro alignment, sensors, level trims, telemetry sensors, black box, ESC telemetry setup, flight controller name; the bank and rates switches. Not included, left untouched: ESC parameters (Scorpion programming), serial ports, LED/OSD/GPS and the receiver's own settings. Restore writes back only what differs (an unchanged setup = reads only, no flash stalls) and verifies every item, restarting the flight controller when the governor or motor block changed; a file from a DIFFERENT model transfers the tune only - your own hardware setup stays. Fixed: the 'back up your proven tune' reminder came far too early - every brief switch-on counted as a flight. Now a flight counts only when it lasted over 3 minutes, and any setup edit (phone or transmitter) clears the count at once. Apps: iOS 4.13, Android 4.05.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.558-backup-review
versions.notes: Backup & restore double-checked before real use (Malcolm's request). The phone backup covers the tuning (PIDs, advanced PIDs, rates, governor, rescue - every bank, plus the governor's global settings), the mechanics (mixer travel/limits/trims, servo centres/travel) and the bank/rates switch assignments; the page and its help now say exactly that and list what is NOT included (arming switch & modes, channel map, motor/gear ratio, battery, filters, telemetry). Pages: Back up shows a warning instead of a tick when the sweep did not finish (and keeps the earlier backup); Restore shows why it stopped; the restore line says whether the backup is your own or the automatic one from connection; importing a different model's file now really leaves your servo/mixer settings alone. Needs app 4.12 (iOS) / 4.04 (Android) for the new fields - the apps fix the real bugs: the flight controller's bank was read from the wrong bytes, so every backup sweep left it on bank 1 instead of where it was; a deliberate backup was overwritten by the automatic one at the next connection; a read that got no answer still produced a tick; restore now checks the FC stayed on the chosen bank after each item, stops if the transmitter comes on, and verifies the EEPROM save. Firmware itself unchanged apart from the pages.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.557-disarm-ble-fast
versions.notes: Faster PID tuning at the field (Malcolm's suggestion): Bluetooth now comes back half a second after you DISARM - the old 5-second wait was a leftover from the WiFi bring-up, which stalls the receiver; restarting Bluetooth does not. So the cycle is arm, fly, land, disarm, edit on the phone, arm again. Arming still switches the radios off 3 s later, on the ground, as before. Home WiFi keeps its 5-second wait after disarm. Firmware only - pages unchanged.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.556-telemetry-guard
versions.notes: Fix + safeguard: after a bank copy the transmitter showed no volts and no RPM - the flight controller's telemetry sensor list and link rate had been wiped (all zero; cause still unknown - the receiver did not write them). Rotorflight only sends the sensors on that list, so an empty list makes a healthy FC mute. The receiver now reads that list after it finds the FC, and if it is empty the Home and Rotorflight pages show a red notice with a one-tap 'Restore telemetry sensors' button (transmitter off - the FC restarts). Copy a bank: the result now pops up so it cannot be missed, and the 'from' caption leads with the bank you picked instead of the bank the FC is on. Pages changed - apps 4.11 / 4.03 carry the same.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.555-copybank-route
versions.notes: Fix: the Copy-a-bank page (Rotorflight > Copy a bank) opened fine in the app but gave 'not found' in a web browser on the receiver's own pages - the firmware was missing the link for it. Firmware only - pages unchanged.
